subject: Multiple sessions and trapping grids, mask

messages.author: de2dc40321c25f45
messages.subject: Multiple sessions and trapping grids, mask
parts:
Hi,


I have a dataset from rodent trapping that includes several trapping sessions in several trapping grids. We trapped monthly for 2 years, with three nights of trapping per occasion = a total of 26 occasions and 6 sessions per occasion. I have 24 trapping grids with 9 – 16 traps per grid (mostly 16 traps). The trapping grids are divided into 3 regions (8 grids at each), and located at different elevations (two levels). Some of the grids are not trapped during winter. The grids are independent from each other as they are located far enough away that they do not detect the same individuals at multiple grids.


My overall goal is to be able to describe the relationship between density and sigma and the elevation covariate per occasion. So I would like to run a model where D and sigma ~occasion*elevation


Does anyone have a good idea how I could do this? And I am particularly thinking of how to build up the mask.


Thank you!


Best,

Kaja

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multiple sessions and trapping grids, mask
parts:
Hi Kaja

This will take some working through... First, maybe we can clarify some things. I think you are using 'occasion' and 'session' with meanings reversed from how I understand them (occasions are intervals or samples within a session) - switching will make it easier to use the 'secr' package, which I assume you intend to do. Were there two trap clearances per day to give 6 occasions per 3-night session? Secondly, it's critical that your grids are not too small (less than a home range in extent) (I expect you addressed that way back when you started).

I haven't seen anyone tackle a problem of that size (24 grids x 26 sessions) in one model, and you may run into trouble just because of the size of the problem. There is no hope of estimating 24 x 26 x 3 parameters in one model fit, but there are much simpler models that do stand a chance. More than 10-15 parameters is a lot in 'secr'. I suggest you start with a simple model and subset of the data.

Suppose each grid x session is nominally a new 'session'. Then you can specify elevation and 'occasion' (month, year, season?) and region as session-level covariates in the model argument of secr.fit (provide the data in sessioncov); this does not require anything in the mask. Temporal (monthly) changes in density can potentially be modelled with regression splines (I've tried it once) which can save a lot of parameters. The same also goes for sigma and lambda0. Or you can test hypotheses involving an inverse relationship between D and sigma with the 'sigmak' parameter - putting some clues together, I am guessing you have heard about that :). If you have just two grid geometries (3 x 3, 4 x 4 square) then in principle you need just two masks (assuming traps are numbered the same on similar grids).  For standard grids there is the option of 'mashing' (overlaying) replicate data sets, which can save a lot of time.

I'm pessimistic that one big model is going to work for you (it may just require too much memory and take too long). Maybe you need to break the problem into a number of separate model fits and defy popular wisdom by doing statistics on the estimates.

That's about the limit of my thoughts - details will depend on poking the data and seeing what works. I hope you don't give up too easily!
Murray
